title: Fail closed on unapproved existing PDF output replacement
description: PDF mutators currently rely on the atomic writer's overwrite behavior for distinct output paths. An existing destination can be replaced without a caller supplying the exact current destination identity that was reviewed and approved. Align runtime enforcement with the workflow contract: new destinations remain easy, same-document mutations retain their separately guarded backup lifecycle, and a distinct existing destination is never replaced unless the call binds the approved current canonical path, byte length, and SHA-256 and the server revalidates that identity immediately before activation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every PDF mutator defaults to no replacement for a distinct output path. 2. Replacing a distinct existing output requires the exact approved current output identity: canonical path, byte length, and SHA-256. 3. The identity is validated while the atomic output lock is held and rechecked before activation; drift fails closed without altering source or destination. 4. New output creation and intentionally supported same-document mutations continue through explicit, separately tested contracts. 5. Batch mutators either bind every existing destination identity or fail the whole batch before staging. 6. Tests cover absent target, matching identity, stale hash, stale length, wrong canonical path, aliasing, target creation races, target mutation races, mixed batches, crash recovery, and all mutator schemas. 7. The pinned PDF.js version and unrelated dependencies do not change. 8. Broad verification runs on Silverbook, Stonebook, or iMac, not Silvercloud.
close_reason: Existing-output replacement now requires exact approved identity and descriptor-bound verification; implementation and exact Silverbook proof are complete.

title: Make all PDF output paths atomic and rollback-safe
description: merge_pdfs, split_pdf, rotate_pdf_pages, reorder_pdf_pages, apply_page_plan, and some bulk paths write directly to final destinations. A write or multi-output failure can truncate an existing output, leave partial files, or advance lifecycle state inconsistently.
design: Route single-output PDF mutations through the canonical same-directory temporary write plus rename path with explicit durability and overwrite policy. Give multi-output split and bulk operations a transaction-like staging and commit contract with rollback or a complete partial-result report. Add injected failures for write, rename, permission, disk-full simulation, and mid-batch errors.
acceptance_criteria: Every PDF-producing handler has a declared atomicity and overwrite policy; injected failures preserve pre-existing output bytes and source bytes; no temporary residue remains; active-document state advances only after successful commit; split and bulk failures either commit the entire declared set or return an exact retained partial set without misreporting success; focused and full regression suites pass.
notes:
2026-07-21 same-document commits now use fsynced same-directory temp files, atomic rename, durable pending/committed journal, per-document interprocess locks, and final optimistic recheck. This materially hardens the path but does not close this bead: merge, split, rotate, reorder, page-plan, and multi-output rollback policies still need the full acceptance matrix.
2026-07-21 selected as the next autonomous lane after the green fidelity milestone. Start with a complete producer/write-path inventory, define overwrite and rollback policy per tool, then implement shared single-output atomic commit and staged multi-output split with injected failure coverage.
Completed in 8b085c7 and integrated by 1181ce5. All user-visible PDF outputs now use staged atomic commits; split and bulk use bounded-memory lazy producers plus whole-set rollback. Fault matrix covers disk-full, permission, write, sync, rename, transient cleanup, collision, concurrent replacement, special-file rejection, batch generation failure, and active-state gating. Full suite passed 519/519; isolated concurrency lanes passed 517 each; share contract passed; final reproducible MCPB was 72,463,976 bytes across 2,821 files with SHA-256 58a535627470c13f094ccb60d169a686f76dbd199c16ac3a210b018d1aee55ac; packed Linux smoke passed 37 tools, 14 prompts, canonical resources, and native raster. pdfjs-dist remained exactly 5.4.624. Abrupt process-death recovery is deliberately tracked separately in pdf-toolkit-mcp-xt6.

title: Preserve original backup identity across deletion and restart
description: Same-path mutation backup identity currently depends on the in-process backupPathByCanonical map. If the remembered backup disappears, ensureBackupForCanonicalPath recreates a new backup from the current possibly mutated PDF and can present it as the original. Restart also loses the mapping.
design: Persist and verify immutable original identity for each canonical document, including original SHA-256 and backup SHA-256. A missing or mismatched original backup must fail closed with an actionable recovery path rather than copying current mutated bytes. Cover H0 to H1 to H2, backup deletion, restart or rehydration, and concurrent access.
acceptance_criteria: The first same-path mutation creates one backup equal to H0; later mutations keep the same path and H0 hash; deleting or tampering with that backup never creates a replacement from H1 or H2 labeled as original; restart or rehydration preserves or safely refuses the relationship; failures do not advance active-document state; tests include exact hashes and independent reopen.
notes: 2026-07-21 fixed in a0e9ba5 and verified at 10d11e0. Durable per-canonical-path H0 record binds backup path, original SHA-256, last committed SHA-256, and pending journal state. Missing/tampered backup, deleted record, legacy evidence, forged rehydration, file/directory symlinks, restart, external replacement, and concurrent mutation all fail closed or preserve one H0 as contracted. The missing-backup campaign passes 3/3. Acceptance met across focused and repeated fidelity evidence.

title: Use explicit Node rendering factories inside Claude Desktop Electron
description: Issues #42 and #43 reproduce undefined document.createElement during PDF rasterization on Windows even when the native canvas package can load. Claude Desktop's Electron utility process can cause pdf.js to choose its browser factories.
design: Pass Node-capable CanvasFactory and FilterFactory behavior explicitly for render document loads rather than relying on pdf.js isNodeJS detection. Preserve macOS system fallback and text-only extraction.
acceptance_criteria: render_pdf_page, render_pdf_region, and scanned read_pdf_content work with Electron-like process.type; no document.createElement path is used; tests reproduce and prevent regression; errors preserve underlying cause.
close_reason: Fixed on master: explicit pdf.js Node CanvasFactory and FilterFactory prevent Electron utility processes from selecting DOM factories. Added utility-process regression coverage for page rendering, region rendering, and scanned-PDF image fallback; 185 tests and UI build pass.

title: Honor MCPB multi-directory configuration on every platform
description: Issue #42 shows Claude Desktop can leave the literal multiple-selection template or otherwise fail to provide a usable ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES environment value. The MCPB spec defines multiple selections as separate command arguments.
design: Add the configured directory array to mcp_config args in both manifests and teach server startup to consume only explicit allow-directory arguments while preserving ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES for other stdio hosts. Reject unresolved templates and deduplicate canonical paths.
acceptance_criteria: Both manifests use the same argument contract; multiple Windows paths including non-C drives work; environment fallback remains compatible; unresolved template tokens cannot silently narrow the allowlist; tests cover POSIX and Windows-style inputs.
close_reason: Implemented MCPB multi-directory argument expansion in both manifests with explicit marker parsing, unresolved-template rejection, environment fallback, canonical deduplication, Windows-path unit coverage, and live MCP transport coverage. Verified 2026-07-21: focused 6/6, full suite 182/182, UI build passed. Clean Windows package validation remains in sibling bead pdf-toolkit-mcp-dwk.3.

title: v0.8.2: Type-aware zone actions (signature / initials / date)
description: Current modal treats all zones as 'stamp a signature' — clicking a DATE zone opens the confirm-signature modal which asks for legal name + consent. Wrong semantics. Date zones should stamp today's date as text. Initials zones should stamp initials (or at least say 'initial' not 'sign' in the attestation).
design: Single mode-aware modal. Visible fields adapt to zone.type. (signature) name+saved-picker+attestation+Sign; (initials) name+saved-picker+'I initial...' attestation+Stamp initials; (date) date-picker (default today)+no name+Insert date. Submit path: signature/initials -> apply_signature (unchanged). date -> new apply_text tool (stamps a text string, no intent required). One signature asset pool — user picks a full-sig vs short-form asset themselves.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] New apply_text server tool + tests
- [ ] Modal adapts fields per zone.type

title: Adversarial review gate — Phase B (viewer sign mode)
description: Phase B adds interactive surface that collects signing intent from users. High risk: bugs could collect the wrong intent, stamp the wrong signature, or silently fail. Needs independent review.
design: Spawn code-reviewer subagent with: viewer diff, specific callouts on (1) pointer event correctness across mouse/trackpad/touch, (2) coord conversion canvas->pdf, (3) modal intent synthesis matches CLI contract, (4) zone state management (re-render after apply), (5) drag gesture UX (cancel on esc, minimum size, no interaction with existing zones), (6) accessibility (keyboard navigation, ARIA). Capture findings as follow-up beads.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Code-reviewer agent run on Phase B diff
- [ ] Findings triaged: blocker / follow-up / rejected
- [ ] Blockers fixed before closing
- [ ] Accessibility gaps filed for v0.8.1 at minimum
- [ ] Any security issues filed as P0
close_reason: Code-reviewer agent run on Phase B viewer diff. 6 blockers identified, all fixed in-session: (B1) drag state now stored in PDF points (scale-invariant) — mid-drag zoom no longer skews zone. (B2) clearZoneOverlay preserves the in-progress drag draft element + updateDraftRectangle re-scales it after renderPage. (B3) .sig-zone[data-applied] set to pointer-events:none in CSS + no click handler bound in renderZoneOverlay — no longer swallows drag-to-create over signed areas. (B4) signingInFlight guard rejects openSignModal and onZoneClick while any apply_signature is pending — no more racing concurrent signs. (B5) isMeaningfulName helper enforces >=3 alphanumeric chars client-side, replacing the trivially-bypassed length >= 2 check; rejects pure-symbol names and zero-width junk. (B6) Quick signature names now have a random 6-char suffix + overwrite:false — shared-machine users with same typed name no longer collide. Plus F4 (stale 'coming soon' copy) and F10 (timestamp regenerated inside try/finally) fixed inline. Remaining review follow-ups (DPR, focus trap, pointerleave stroke split, accessibility, caching, error state) filed as pdf-toolkit-mcp-<see follow-up bead>. UI build clean, 140/140 tests green.

title: Viewer sign-mode: drag-to-create custom zone
description: When detect_signature_zones misses a spot, user should be able to drag a rectangle on the PDF to create a custom zone, then sign it via the same modal.
design: Pointer-down on empty PDF area (not over an existing zone) -> pointermove draws preview rectangle -> pointerup finalizes zone with auto-detected type 'signature' (user can change via modal). Zone added to state array, rendered like detected zones. Same modal flow triggers on click. Custom zones persist in viewer state only (not written to PDF until Sign).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Pointer-down on empty area starts drag
- [ ] Preview rect shown during drag
- [ ] Pointer-up creates zone at drag bounds
- [ ] Minimum dimensions enforced (>=20x10 pts to prevent tiny accidental zones)
- [ ] Custom zone clickable like detected ones
- [ ] Esc cancels in-progress drag
close_reason: Pointer-based drag-to-create on zone-layer. page-wrapper gets .mode-sign class which enables pointer-events on zone-layer + crosshair cursor. Pointerdown on empty area (e.target not inside a sig-zone) starts the drag, preview rect (.sig-zone-draft) updates during pointermove, pointerup creates a SignatureZone with source='user-drag' and auto-opens the confirm modal. Minimum 20×10 pts enforced; smaller drags treated as clicks. Escape cancels in-progress drag. Coordinates converted CSS->PDF-points by dividing by scale. UI build clean, 140/140 tests green.

title: Viewer sign-mode: drawing canvas with pointer events (mouse + touch)
description: Let users draw their signature directly in the viewer and save it as a reusable asset. Uses pointer events for unified mouse / trackpad / touch support.
design: New 'Draw signature' button in sign mode toolbar. Opens a canvas modal with drawing surface. PointerEvent-based stroke capture: pointerdown -> start path, pointermove -> line to current point, pointerup -> close path. Stroke style: black, 2px, round cap. Undo button (stroke stack). Save button exports canvas to PNG dataURL -> calls create_signature(name, image_data_url). Clear button resets canvas. Touch-specific: touch-action:none on canvas to prevent scroll.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Drawing canvas modal
- [ ] Pointer events work for mouse, trackpad, touch
- [ ] touch-action:none prevents page scroll during draw
- [ ] Undo stroke stack
- [ ] Clear resets
- [ ] Save exports to PNG data URL + calls create_signature
- [ ] Signature appears in list_signatures after save
close_reason: Draw-signature modal with HTML5 canvas capturing strokes via PointerEvents (unified mouse/trackpad/touch). touch-action:none prevents page scroll during draw. Undo (pop last stroke) + Clear (reset) + Save (exports canvas toDataURL -> calls create_signature with image_data_url). Strokes stored as arrays of [x,y] points for clean undo/redraw. White background ensures saved PNG is legible. Integrates with confirm modal: when a user draws + saves while the confirm modal is open, the new signature auto-populates the 'use existing' dropdown. UI build clean, 140/140 tests green.

title: Viewer sign-mode: confirm modal + intent synthesis
description: Click on a zone opens a modal that collects the typed name, previews the attestation sentence, and calls apply_signature on confirm. The viewer synthesizes user_intent_statement + user_confirmed_at from the click — keeping the CLI-path contract intact while providing better UX.
design: Modal shows: document filename + page + zone label, 'Type your full name' input, live preview of 'I, {typed}, sign {filename} on {today-iso-date}.', Cancel + Sign buttons (Sign disabled until name matches a saved signature's display_name OR exceeds 3 chars). On Sign: captures timestamp, calls apply_signature with intent values synthesized from the click. Re-snapshots zones after success (applied zone disappears from overlay, stamped image visible on canvas).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Modal component with name input + statement preview + buttons
- [ ] Synthesizes user_intent_statement from typed name + filename
- [ ] user_confirmed_at = click timestamp
- [ ] Disabled Sign button until name is entered
- [ ] Calls apply_signature via app.callServerTool
- [ ] Re-renders PDF after success to show applied signature
- [ ] Cancel closes without side effect
close_reason: Modal HTML in ui/index.html (backdrop + content + form fields + attestation preview + actions). CSS in ui/src/mcp-app.css (~180 lines). TypeScript: openSignModal / closeSignModal / populateSavedSignatures (lists saved sigs from list_signatures) / updateStatementPreview (live-updates as user types) / onConfirmSign (creates quick-{name} signature if needed, calls apply_signature with synthesized intent, marks zone applied, shows toast). Esc + backdrop-click cancel. Output saved to {original}-signed.pdf. UI build clean, 140/140 tests green. Next: 3d9 drawing canvas, d10 drag-to-create, then a5t review gate.

title: Viewer sign-mode: toggle + zone overlay rendering
description: Viewer needs a third mode (view / manage / sign). In sign mode, calls detect_signature_zones on load and renders each zone as a colored dashed rectangle over the PDF canvas — signatures blue, initials amber, dates gray.
design: Extend ManageMode type to include 'sign'. Add Sign tab next to View/Manage. On entering sign mode: call app.callServerTool detect_signature_zones with current pdfPath. Store result in zones state. Render overlay via absolutely-positioned divs over the PDF canvas (scales with zoom). Each zone gets cursor pointer + hover highlight + click handler. Include empty-state when zero zones detected ('No signature zones detected — drag on the PDF to create one').
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Sign tab added to mode toolbar
- [ ] detect_signature_zones called on entering mode
- [ ] Zones render as positioned dashed rects over PDF
- [ ] Color-coded by type (blue/amber/gray)
- [ ] Zones scale correctly when user zooms
- [ ] Hover state + click handler
- [ ] Empty state when zero zones
close_reason: Added 'Sign' tab to mode toolbar, <zone-layer> div inside page-wrapper for absolutely-positioned overlays, <sign-panel> sidebar with zone list + status + type legend. TypeScript: extended ManageMode to include 'sign', added SignatureZone interface + signatureZones state, fetchSignatureZones() via app.callServerTool detect_signature_zones on mode entry, renderZoneOverlay() rendering dashed rectangles color-coded by type (signature=blue, initials=amber, date=gray), scaling with zoom, with per-zone click handlers. Empty state handled in sign panel. Click handler placeholder logs + highlights — modal wiring is in bead pdf-toolkit-mcp-zeg. UI build clean, 140/140 tests green.

title: Adversarial review gate — Phase A (zone detection)
description: Phase A touches security-adjacent surface (coordinate-driven signature placement, user-facing tool with forgeable intent). Needs independent review before it unlocks Phase B.
design: Spawn code-reviewer subagent with: diff since last closed bead, specific callouts on (1) zone coord conversion correctness, (2) detection false-positive rate, (3) tool description phrasing resistance to agent misuse, (4) test coverage gaps. Capture findings as follow-up beads. Block Phase B start until this gate closes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Code-reviewer agent run on Phase A diff
- [ ] Findings triaged: blocker / follow-up / rejected
- [ ] Blockers fixed before closing
- [ ] Follow-ups filed as new beads
close_reason: Code-reviewer agent run on Phase A diff. 4 blockers identified, all fixed in-session before closing gate: (1) AcroForm field-name regex tightened to require non-letter boundary [(^|[^a-z])(sig|signature)s?(?![a-z]) / same pattern for initials] — rejects 'Initialize', 'Resignation', 'Assignment' while matching snake_case like 'form_sig1'. (2) Page rotation handled by forcing getViewport({rotation:0}) so text coords stay in native space consistent with pdf-lib's widget rectangles. (3) Bare-word patterns ^Signature$ / ^Initials?$ / ^Date$ now require empty horizontal space to the right (30-40pt), with single-char decorative glyphs (▶ ☑ etc.) ignored in the room check — kills section-header false positives without losing W-9's Date zone. (4) apply_signature description rewritten: EXCEPTION clause removed, 'NEVER FABRICATE' elevated to uppercase start-of-description, viewer-drag trust moved to Phase B via a dedicated channel marker (to be added in sign-mode wiring). Typo fix (test title 1/7 -> 1/3) also landed. Follow-ups filed as beads: 2nxj7m1 (labels + types + dedup + encrypted + golden thresholds), plus polish + rotated-fixture beads. 140/140 tests green.

title: Strengthen apply_signature description to require zone detection first
description: Current apply_signature description lets agents pick arbitrary coordinates. Proven failure mode: our W-9 demo put the signature on the General Instructions section. Description should explicitly instruct agents: always call detect_signature_zones first, apply at a returned zone, do not guess.
design: Rewrite description to lead with 'First call detect_signature_zones and apply only at a returned zone. Guessing coordinates will place the signature in the wrong location.' Add example chain in description. Note exception: user-drag-placed from viewer (legitimate user intent to pick spot manually).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Description rewritten
- [ ] Example chain included
- [ ] Clarifies viewer-drag exception
- [ ] All existing tests still pass
close_reason: apply_signature description rewritten with explicit REQUIRED WORKFLOW: (1) call detect_signature_zones first, (2) pick matching zone, (3) elicit user_intent_statement + user_confirmed_at from user, (4) call apply_signature. Never-guess rule made prominent. Viewer-drag exception documented.

title: Golden-set signature placement eval harness
description: Without a reproducible eval we can't prove detect_signature_zones works or catch regressions. Mirrors Shopify's autoresearch pattern at small scale (reference memory: reference_autoresearch_eval_pattern.md).
design: test/fixtures/golden-forms/ with 5 real PDFs: IRS W-9 (AcroForm signature field), IRS I-9 (multi-signer), Sandy Springs Business License (flat form), public mutual NDA (initials-per-page), standard rental application (sig+date pair). expected.json maps each form to hand-labeled ground-truth zones. test/signature-zones-placement.test.js runs detect_signature_zones on each fixture, computes IoU vs ground truth, reports per-form score + aggregate. Ship gate: >=80% of zones hit IoU>=0.5 (loosens to 0.3 for initials). Test auto-skips if OFFLINE=1 when fetching online fixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] 5 fixtures committed (or fetched from known URLs)
- [ ] expected.json ground truth hand-labeled
- [ ] IoU scoring helper with union/intersection math
- [ ] Test reports per-form scores + aggregate
- [ ] Ship gate >=80% IoU>=0.5
- [ ] Fixtures include at least one failure case for initials detection
- [ ] Runs in <10s
close_reason: test/fixtures/golden-forms/expected.json with 2 fixtures (example-fw9 local, irs-fw9-2024 via URL fetch-on-demand). Ground truth as x_min/x_max/y_min/y_max regions (not exact boxes — text-heuristic is fuzzy by design). Hit criterion: type+page match AND (IoU>=min_iou OR fully contained). Run OFFLINE=1 to skip URL fixtures. Both fixtures currently score 1.00 on min_score 0.5 gate. Report printed per-run for visibility.

title: Build detect_signature_zones helper + tool
description: Agents currently stamp signatures at arbitrary coordinates because they have no way to locate the actual sign-here spot (proven: W-9 test put signature on General Instructions, not the signature line). New tool returns a typed-zone list so agents never guess coordinates again.
design: Layered detection in helpers.js: (1) AcroForm signature-typed fields -> confidence 0.99 via form.getFields filter; (2) AcroForm text fields named like /sig|initial/i -> 0.85; (3) pdfjs text extraction with bounding boxes -> scan for 'Signature of', 'Sign Here', 'Initial', 'Date:' patterns -> 0.70-0.90 per pattern; (4) adjacent rectangle detection for initials boxes -> 0.75. Returns array of { type, label, page, x, y, width, height, confidence, source } with top-left origin coords. New tool detect_signature_zones wired in server/index.js.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] extractPdfTextWithBounds helper converts pdfjs transforms to top-left coords
- [ ] detectSignatureZones helper returns typed-zone array
- [ ] detect_signature_zones MCP tool exposed
- [ ] Multi-page PDFs return zones for every page
- [ ] AcroForm case uses form fields directly (high confidence)
- [ ] Text-heuristic case works on flat PDFs
- [ ] Unit tests for each detection layer
- [ ] No false-positive on PDFs with no signatures
close_reason: Built three helpers in server/helpers.js: computeIoU (IoU math), extractPdfTextWithBounds (pdfjs text items with top-left origin coords), detectSignatureZones (layered detection: AcroForm signature fields conf 0.99, AcroForm sig/initials-named text fields 0.85, text-heuristic patterns 0.65-0.92). New MCP tool detect_signature_zones wired in server/index.js. Dedup via IoU 0.4 threshold. 19 new unit tests. Live-tested via MCP protocol: IRS W-9 returns 2 zones (signature + date), both at correct locations, with the false-positive 'Signature requirements.' on page 5 successfully suppressed after tightening patterns.

title: Warn loudly on XFA forms instead of silent data loss
description: pdf-lib strips XFA form data when it saves any XFA PDF. Common in government/IRS forms (Sandy Springs business license is likely one). Currently we silently gut the form. User has no idea why their form stopped working.
design: Detect XFA by checking AcroForm dict for /XFA key before any mutation. If present, emit a warning in tool response and, where appropriate, throw unless force:true. Apply to: fill_pdf, apply_signature, add_signature_field, prepare_signing_packet, apply_page_plan. Non-mutating tools (read_pdf_fields, get_pdf_info) can continue.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] hasXfaForm(pdfDoc) helper
- [ ] Mutating tools warn when XFA detected
- [ ] Warning includes next-step guidance ('this form uses XFA; our tools cannot preserve XFA data — convert to AcroForm first')
- [ ] Test with a known XFA form fixture
close_reason: Added detectXfaForm(pdfBytes) helper (raw-byte heuristic, scans first 200KB for /XFA pattern). Wired into apply_signature, add_signature_field, prepare_signing_packet — all refuse on XFA detection unless force_xfa=true opt-in. 4 tests: AcroForm returns false, synthetic XFA returns true, empty/tiny inputs return false, no false-positive on /XYZ or /XObject. Follow-up bead pdf-toolkit-mcp-c5t for extending to fill_pdf / bulk_fill_from_csv / apply_page_plan (existing tools — scope-separated to avoid regression risk in v0.8.0).

title: Detect and refuse to stamp over existing crypto signatures
description: apply_signature currently silently invalidates any existing cryptographic signature on the input PDF (pdf-lib round-trip breaks them). User thinks they added a signature; they actually destroyed a legally-binding one.
design: Before apply_signature touches the PDF, scan for /Sig entries in AcroForm. If present, throw a clear error unless allow_resign:true is passed. Prefer pdf-lib's form.getFields() filtering for SignatureField types. Document in tool description.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] hasExistingSignature(pdfDoc) helper in helpers.js
- [ ] apply_signature refuses by default if signature fields exist
- [ ] allow_resign:true opt-in bypasses the check
- [ ] Error message tells user what was detected and why
- [ ] Test with a digitally-signed fixture PDF
close_reason: Added detectExistingSignatures(pdfDoc) helper that scans form fields for PDFSignature-type entries. apply_signature now refuses when present, unless allow_resign=true opt-in. 3 tests: unsigned PDF returns false, mock signed PDF returns true with field names, missing-form case handled gracefully.

title: Fix redirect-based SSRF in fetch_pdf_from_url
description: fetch currently uses redirect:'follow' which bypasses isPrivateHost check — a public URL can 302 to 169.254.169.254 (AWS metadata) and we follow it. Real vulnerability.
design: Switch to manual redirect following. On each hop: parse Location header, re-validate isPrivateHost unless allow_private_hosts=true, cap at 5 hops, preserve existing UX for public-CDN redirects. Add test: fake fetch that returns 302→private-host, assert rejection.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] downloadPdfFromUrl follows redirects manually
- [ ] isPrivateHost check runs on every hop
- [ ] Redirect loop cap at 5 hops
- [ ] Test: 302 to 169.254.169.254 is rejected
- [ ] Test: 302 to another public host still succeeds
- [ ] All existing fetch tests still pass
close_reason: Manual redirect following with per-hop isPrivateHost validation. Added 7 tests covering: reject redirect to 169.254.169.254, reject redirect to localhost, reject redirect to RFC1918, allow public-to-public redirect, reject redirect loops > maxRedirects, resolve relative Location headers, never write a file on rejected redirect. Return payload now includes finalUrl + redirectHops. Default maxRedirects=5.

title: E1: emit MATH_NOT_RECONSTRUCTED typed gap for dropped equations
description: HIGHEST LEVERAGE. 71.8% of the bench's 3,385 math tests fail SILENTLY because there is no gap code for 'equations not reconstructed' — we drop equations without declaring it, violating our own fail-closed standard. Add MATH_NOT_RECONSTRUCTED to GAP_CODES in server/markdown-conversion.js (currently 17 codes, ~line 64) and emit it per page when math-bearing source content is detected but not represented in the Markdown. Must be evidence-backed (do not guess): candidate signals already available in the IR are math-class text items, Type-3/Computer-Modern glyph groups, and the existing math-run detection used by the bounded log-spacing repair. Fail-closed discipline unchanged: this DECLARES a limit, it does not attempt reconstruction. Expected effect: converts ~2,400 silent failures into declared limits, moving overall silent from 45.2% toward ~11%.
acceptance_criteria: MATH_NOT_RECONSTRUCTED registered in GAP_CODES and in the output schema enum; emitted per page only on evidence of unrepresented math content, never speculatively; LIMITATIONS prose updated; no change to reconstruction behavior (byte-identical Markdown body); fixtures cover positive (equations present, gap emitted) and negative (no math, no gap); share-mirror parity; re-run bench shows math silent-rate collapse.
notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION (verified 2026-08-19): the converter ALREADY declares this limit in prose — a '## Conversion limitations' section ships in 95.2% of outputs (1336/1403) stating 'General equations, subscripts, other fraction bars... remain source reading-order text rather than being guessed.' So 'we drop equations without declaring it' is WRONG; do not repeat it. The accurate gap is narrower: the limit is global PROSE, not a PER-PAGE TYPED gap, so a consumer cannot tell which pages actually lost math and no machine can route on it. E1 = make an existing prose limitation machine-readable and page-specific. The three-bucket metric measures TYPED-GAP COVERAGE, not disclosure; define 'silent' precisely as 'not covered by a typed gap' whenever the report card is published.
E1 MEASURED ON REAL MATH (2026-08-19, control tower, 338 bench PDFs across 4 categories, 0 conversion errors). FIRING: arxiv_math 33/120 = 27.5%; old_scans_math 0/36 = 0.0% BUT 36/36 were already covered by TEXT_LAYER_EMPTY/OCR_NOT_PERFORMED so no gap was needed there (correct behaviour, not a miss). FALSE-POSITIVE CONTROLS: headers_footers 1/120 = 0.8%; long_tiny_text 0/62 = 0.0%. VERDICT: precision excellent, coverage PARTIAL. Honest impact estimate: overall silent 45.2% -> ~33.8%, NOT the ~11% projected in the epic (that assumed full math coverage). Correcting the epic's projection. Two documented coverage caps explain the shortfall, both failing safe (silence, never a fabricated gap): (1) the named-operator branch reuses the codebase's existing CAPITALISED Lim|Max|Min|sum|int|infinity vocabulary, so real papers' lowercase lim/max/min do not match; (2) the run-shape gate requires every structural item to be a single character, math punctuation, or 'log', so displayed equations arriving as one merged text item emit nothing. Broadening either is an evidence change deserving its own review — do NOT fold it into this lane. Gates re-verified by control tower: math-gap 6/6, convert+markdown 98/98, share parity green; diff scope clean, share mirrors byte-identical, Markdown body byte-identical across 14 pre-change baselines.

title: Stop asserting unverified metadata through merge and split
description:
Measured defect, not a feature gap. Splitting a merged document stamps the merged file Info onto every output regardless of which pages it contains, so a range consisting entirely of the second input pages positively asserts the FIRST input author.

Measured through the MCP boundary on 2026-07-25: inputs A (Title A / Author A) and B (Title B / Author B), merged, then split at the original source boundary. Output pages_3-4 contains only B pages and reports Title A / Author A / Subject A / kw-A. Regression coverage is already committed in test/metadata-provenance.test.js, where the assertions marked CURRENT pin this behavior.

For a tool used on contracts and forms, misattributed authorship is worse than absent metadata. A user who merges a counterparty document with their own, splits it, and returns a range is shipping a file whose stated authorship is wrong, with nothing marking the claim as inherited.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR, per the decision record in docs/METADATA_PROVENANCE.md:
- merge_pdfs must not present one input Title/Author/Subject/Keywords as describing the whole. Where inputs disagree, OMIT the field rather than pick the first.
- split_pdf must not copy document metadata onto ranges whose provenance it cannot establish.
- Omission over false assertion, matching the existing rule that incomplete page analysis reports unknown rather than likely_blank and form validation refuses whole-form readiness claims it cannot support.

Do NOT add PieceInfo or any private page dictionary as part of this. That is rejected permanently in the decision record.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The CURRENT assertions in test/metadata-provenance.test.js are inverted: the second split range must no longer claim Author A.
- Single-input merge and ordinary split of an unmerged document keep their metadata, since provenance is unambiguous there.
- Output schema and tool contract updated if the result surfaces what was dropped.
notes: 2026-07-28 partial milestone: multi-input merge_pdfs now preserves each descriptive field only on unanimous valid consensus, reports omitted fields, and retains single-input metadata (implementation commit 6cedf0d before integration). The split-side requirement remains unresolved. A proper-subset split cannot distinguish an ordinary single-source PDF from a heterogeneous or externally merged PDF using document-level metadata alone. Private page provenance markers are explicitly disallowed, while stripping metadata from every proper-subset split conflicts with the acceptance requirement that ordinary unmerged splits retain metadata. Human product-policy decision required: either omit descriptive metadata for all proper-subset splits, or accept and document that foreign heterogeneous PDFs cannot be detected without provenance evidence. apply_page_plan can also delete pages and should follow the same eventual rule.

title: Reconcile viewer overlay coordinates with the canonical page box
description:
Found while completing the server-side vk8 normalization; deliberately scoped out because it needs a UI build plus browser smoke evidence that the VM cannot produce.

ui/src/mcp-app.ts nativeRectToViewportRect() builds a pdfRect from zone coordinates and passes it to PDF.js convertToViewportRectangle(), which expects ABSOLUTE user-space coordinates. Two distinct defects:

1. Missing origin. currentNativePageHeight() reads currentViewport.viewBox but uses only its height (viewBox[3] - viewBox[1]) and never its origin (viewBox[0], viewBox[1]). Zone coordinates are box-relative, so overlays are displaced by the page box origin on any page whose origin is nonzero. Same class as the server defect fixed in commit 8c34046.

2. Reference-box mismatch (pre-existing, deeper). PDF.js viewBox is the VIEW (CropBox intersected with MediaBox), while the server canon is the MediaBox — established by commit 4ebbaeb, which deliberately derived detector dimensions from MediaBox rather than the PDF.js CropBox viewport, and by the accepted golden fixture. For the golden rotated-signature fixture (MediaBox [0 0 480 360], CropBox [20 24 430 300]) the viewer computes with height 276 while the server emits coordinates against height 360, so overlay placement and detected zones disagree by the CropBox inset even when the origin is zero.

Do not fix (1) alone: adding the viewBox origin while the height still comes from the CropBox would mix two reference boxes and could move overlays that currently render acceptably.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decide and document one reference box for the viewer, consistent with the server MediaBox canon.
- Apply origin and dimensions from that single box together.
- Prove with the existing browser smoke lanes on a Mac host: smoke:ui-sign, smoke:ui-sign-rotated, smoke:ui-preview-zone, smoke:ui-name-zone.
- Add a nonzero-origin MediaBox fixture to the UI smoke set; current fixtures are all origin [0 0].
- Re-verify the accepted rotated/cropped golden (expected zone [72 181 240 18], score 1.0) does not regress.
notes:
2026-07-25 Claude: closed. Both defects fixed; the viewer now uses the same page box the server measures zones against.

ROOT CAUSE. Zones cross the MCP boundary as top-left origin points relative to each page MediaBox, but PDF.js never exposes the MediaBox: viewport.viewBox is the VIEW (CropBox intersected with MediaBox). The viewer flipped y using viewBox height and passed the result to convertToViewportRectangle, which expects ABSOLUTE user space. Wrong twice on any page where the boxes differ: cropped height, and box origin dropped. On the accepted golden fixture (MediaBox [0 0 480 360], CropBox [20 24 430 300]) that is 84pt vertical displacement plus a 20pt horizontal inset, on an entirely ordinary page shape.

FIX. detect_signature_zones now returns REQUIRED page_geometry (per-page MediaBox origin + dimensions), since the viewer cannot derive it. Conversions extracted to ui/src/page-box.ts: zoneToPdfRect (zone -> absolute) and pdfPointToZonePoint (absolute -> zone, for hand-dragged zones). Both directions fixed together; correcting one alone leaves drawing and pointer reading disagreeing while a detect-then-place round trip still looks correct. resolvePageBox prefers server geometry, falls back to viewBox only for early-load states.

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE RESULT. The browser smoke lanes CANNOT catch this. They build fixtures from example-fw9.pdf with at most a rotation, so MediaBox origin is (0,0) with no CropBox. Reverting the viewer fix, rebuilding, and rerunning smoke:ui-sign-rotated produced BYTE-IDENTICAL output across all three rotations. test/viewer-page-box.test.ts is the real gate: 3 of its 10 assertions fail against the pre-fix math. All four zone smoke lanes (sign, sign-rotated, preview-zone, name-zone) pass as regression cover, run on this VM via agent-browser with AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS=--no-sandbox (AppArmor blocks unprivileged user namespaces here; the committed harness was NOT weakened).

CONTRACT RIPPLE, all resolved. The tool-contract digest moved deliberately (previous value recorded beside the new one). The Phase 1 layout oracle binds server/output-schemas.js in its source closure and correctly refused regeneration; regenerated with ONLY the source fingerprint changing and zero layout data, confirming the schema edit does not affect extraction. Share bundle mirrored byte-for-byte including dist-ui.

Full suite 1217 passed, 0 failed. Documented in docs/MAINTAINERS.md, including the warning that smoke lanes do not cover this class.

title: Bind output transaction recovery to canonical directory identity
description: writePdfOutputsAtomic and its output-side recovery remain pathname-based. A deterministic ancestor substitution after directory validation can redirect recovery into a substituted directory, mutate its targets, and only fail after the mutation. Apply the input-recovery continuity model to output-writer recovery without weakening atomicity or crash recovery.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Bind the canonical output directory and stable device/inode before recovery or commit mutation
- [ ] Enforce the expected directory identity and allowed-path policy inside lock acquisition, recovery, and immediately before every pathname mutation
- [ ] Deterministic entry and interior swap phases leave the substituted tree byte-for-byte unchanged and the original transaction recoverable
- [ ] Preserve all atomic output, crash recovery, rollback, concurrent writer, and source/share behavior
- [ ] Document the portable Node final-syscall race boundary without claiming it is eliminated
- [ ] Independent adversarial review reports no P0/P1/P2
notes:
Implemented and integrated as ad0a927 from independently reviewed exact candidate feb961dcced0677bbc8e251d9a7989291f51b17f. Output transactions now bind canonical directory identity and allowed-path policy through lock, journal, stage, activation, rollback, cleanup, standalone recovery, Markdown, download, and packaged-share paths. Journal, owner, stage, target, and rollback artifacts carry stable identity plus exact digest where required. Same-byte different-inode substitutions fail closed. title: Build a reproducible current-QPDF WASM encryption adapter

Enforce owner-password or exact modifyforms/modifyassembly/modifyother capability. Defer merge until its multi-input encryption policy is explicit.

title: Make validate_pdf report field completeness truthfully

Root cause of the confusion: Claude Desktop assigns the install directory name, and installing the current MCPB creates local.mcpb.open-document-alliance.pdf-toolkit BESIDE the Directory install ant.dir.gh.silverstein.pdf-filler-simple rather than replacing it. title: Establish a PDF accessibility evaluation and claim-safety gate
description: Turn accessibility from a feature idea into a measured workflow. Separate formal machine-verifiable PDF/UA checks, heuristics, repair guidance, and required human review so PDF Tools never overstates compliance.
design: Use veraPDF as an external standards anchor where feasible, build fixtures with known tag/reading-order/language/form-label/table/alternate-text defects, map outputs to PDF/UA and relevant WCAG techniques, and evaluate report accuracy and repair guidance. Treat certification/legal-compliance wording as a human-gated claim.
acceptance_criteria: Known-good and known-defect fixtures exist; formal validator results and PDF Tools findings are compared; false positives/negatives are measured by rule family; report distinguishes formal failures, heuristics, untested requirements, and human checks; user-facing language cannot claim certification or complete compliance from a partial scan.
notes:
2026-07-25 Claude, second pass: closed the remaining half of the recorded non-blocking hardening, and produced the project's first REAL formal accessibility evidence.

Installed the pinned toolchain on silvercloud. Important correction to the earlier plan: the contract pins OpenJDK21U-jre_x64_LINUX_hotspot with java_binary_sha256 bound to that exact binary, so the evaluation is Linux x64 bound. The MacBook (arm64 macOS) is the WRONG host for this bead; a macOS aarch64 Temurin would fail pinnedArtifactsMatch. RAM was never the blocker, only a missing runtime. Install lives outside the repo at ~/.local/share/pdf-tools-accessibility.

All five pinned digests matched the contract exactly: JRE archive, java binary, veraPDF installer zip, installed wrapper, installed CLI jar. veraPDF 1.30.2 ran correctly on the hardened PATH from the previous pass, which independently validates that /usr/local/bin removal against the real tool rather than only the stub.

First real formal run: passed=true, version_identification TP=1 TN=1 FP=0 FN=0, harness_failures=0. This independently reproduces the Phase 0 pilot result with real tooling. Claim boundary unchanged and still explicit: signature_verification=not_verified_no_trusted_key, and PDF/UA, WCAG, legal compliance, and certification all remain not_established.

Tree binding added. Previously five files were pinned out of 336 tree entries; the other 331 were unbound, so adding a jar beside the pinned one or editing config/validator.xml changed the evidence while every pinned hash still matched. validator.installed_tree_sha256 and runtime.installed_tree_sha256 now bind the complete listing of both trees: every file by content hash, every directory, every symlink by raw target, walked without following. Absolute and escaping symlink targets are rejected outright. Symlinks cannot be rejected wholesale because the pinned JRE has 145 legitimate relative links under legal/. Cost is about 0.6s.

Tamper-proven with controls on both ends, all four cases previously accepted: extra jar in bin/, edited validator.xml, edited JRE file, escaping symlink. Controls passed before and after. Seven synthetic-tree regression tests added so the gate runs with no install present. Focused 95/95; full suite 1191 passed with only the two pre-existing frozen v3 SKILL.md failures.

Install and digest-regeneration procedure documented in docs/ACCESSIBILITY_EVALUATION.md; it was previously absent, so the pilot was not reproducible by anyone else. Evidence retained privately at evidence/accessibility-formal-run-2026-07-25.json bound to commit 9bdda31.

STILL OPEN: trusted signing key for release-signature verification, broader rule-family corpus beyond version_identification, licensed human checklist, assistive-technology review, calibrated repair guidance.

title: Build visual and semantic fidelity graders for PDF mutations

Establish expected-change regions so a successful requested edit does not conceal unrelated drift.
acceptance_criteria: Representative mutation families have before/after oracle data; expected and forbidden change regions are encoded; outputs open in at least two independent engines; pixel/structural thresholds are documented and calibrated; same-path backup and active-document invariants are scored; release output includes visual evidence for failures.

title: Evaluate and adopt MCP 2026-07-28 when Claude Desktop MCPB supports it
description: The next MCP core revision is scheduled for 2026-07-28 and is explicitly breaking. Evaluate it after the final spec, TypeScript SDK v2, and Claude Desktop/MCPB host support are available; upgrade PDF Tools only when local stdio bundle compatibility is demonstrated.
design: Read the final 2026-07-28 spec and changelog, then test version negotiation and MCP Apps extension behavior in a packed PDF Tools MCPB. Assess the stateless core, first-class extensions, JSON Schema 2020-12 tool schemas, deprecations, and any SDK v2 migration. Keep the current production SDK if Claude Desktop or MCPB has not adopted the revision; document the compatibility decision and retest trigger instead of forcing an upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: Final spec and changelog reviewed; final TypeScript SDK v2 status verified; Claude Desktop/MCPB advertised protocol and extension capabilities captured; tools, resources, app UI, structured results, and stdio lifecycle pass in a packed extension; conformance tests pass where applicable; upgrade is shipped only if host-compatible, otherwise a dated deferral decision and next trigger are recorded.
notes:
2026-07-28 Claude: assessed on publication day. Assessment in docs/MCP_2026-07-28_ASSESSMENT.md. RECOMMENDATION: do not adopt yet. No code changed.

GATES. Final spec published: MET. TypeScript SDK v2: MET with a caveat, it did NOT ship as sdk@2 but as new packages @modelcontextprotocol/server and /client, both 2.0.0 at 2026-07-28 00:03 UTC, while monolithic @modelcontextprotocol/sdk stays v1 at 1.30.0. Adoption is a dependency REPLACEMENT and a bootstrap rewrite, not a bump. Claude Desktop / MCPB host support: NOT MET, MCPB unchanged at 2.1.2, Claude Desktop 1.24012.9 on the maintainer host does not log a negotiated protocol version so support cannot be confirmed by inspection. Local stdio bundle compatibility: not started, blocked on the host gate.

CORRECTION TO THE COMMON FRAMING. Press coverage calls this a stateless rewrite aimed at remote HTTP, which is incomplete for a local server. Two items reach stdio directly: (1) the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake is removed at the PROTOCOL level, not the transport level, with protocol version and client capabilities now carried per-request in _meta; (2) servers MUST implement server/discover, which the spec explicitly names as the stdio backward-compatibility probe.

OUR DEPRECATION EXPOSURE IS ZERO. Verified in code: the server declares only tools, resources, prompts. It has never declared Roots, Sampling, or Logging, all three now deprecated. Diagnostics already go to stderr, which is exactly the migration the spec recommends in place of Logging. Transport is stdio, so the HTTP+SSE reclassification, sessions, sticky routing, and Mcp-Session-Id are all inapplicable. No forced migration pressure.

CONCRETE WORK IF WE ADOPT: implement server/discover; add required resultType to every result; add required ttlMs and cacheScope to tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/read, all four of which this server implements; deterministic tools/list ordering; move RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_ERROR_CODE from -32002 to -32602 (server/index.js:1691); replace the SDK dependency.

WHY WAITING IS FREE. Clients MUST treat results omitting resultType as complete; v2 servers speak both 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28; the new feature lifecycle policy guarantees at least twelve months before any deprecated feature can be removed. Advertising a revision the installed host does not speak is a regression, and this project already knows that failure mode from the PDF.js Electron breakage where server-side tests stayed green.

ADOPT WHEN: MCPB ships a 2026-07-28 packaging or Claude Desktop is confirmed to negotiate it; the exact packaged bundle demonstrates discovery, tool invocation, and viewer rendering on a clean current host; and the required changes land behind the usual evidence gates.

SEPARATE, LOWER RISK: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 to 1.30.0 is a v1-line minor bump unrelated to this revision. Evaluate on its own with host validation, do not fold it into a protocol migration.

title: Rehydrate active document state from viewer session
description: After Claude/Desktop restart or MCP reinstall, the viewer can still have a PDF open while get_active_document returns no active document because server-side in-memory state was reset. Add a lightweight set_active_document/sync_active_document tool and have the viewer call it whenever a PDF is loaded or the app reconnects so active state reflects the visible document without requiring the agent to redisplay the file manually.

title: Unify canonical document lifecycle for sign/fill flows
description: Replace the current copy-on-write working-copy model with a canonical-path lifecycle better suited for agents: (1) the opened document path stays canonical, (2) first mutation creates a backup under ~/.pdf-toolkit-files/backups/, (3) subsequent sign/fill/date mutations write back to the canonical file without requiring overwrite flags from the agent, (4) every mutating tool returns active_path and backup_path when relevant, (5) viewer/model/widget context expose the canonical active path, and (6) add a get_active_document tool so agents can recover current document state without guessing. This should eliminate split-identity bugs where signing creates a separate file and later fill operations accidentally target the original.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed in commit e91a548; canonical document path now stays stable across sign/fill flows, first in-place mutation creates a backup under ~/.pdf-toolkit-files/backups/, viewer/model context expose the active path and backup, get_active_document tool added, and sign/date viewer flows now mutate the canonical file instead of creating a separate working-copy identity.

title: Fix detached ArrayBuffer on working-copy reload
description: Viewer reload after stamping to the same -signed.pdf working-copy path can reuse stale cached byte ranges keyed only by path+offset. On a subsequent same-path overwrite, PDF.js hits 'Cannot perform Construct on a detached ArrayBuffer', the viewer toast says refresh failed, and the fallback reloads the original PDF. Fix by invalidating cached range entries/inflight requests for the stamped path before reloading the overwritten working copy; add regression coverage around cache eviction behavior.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed in commit 45ba16b; viewer now invalidates per-path byte-range cache epochs before reloading an overwritten working copy, preventing stale chunk reuse and detached ArrayBuffer errors on same-path -signed.pdf refreshes.

title: Vite dev mode for the viewer — mocked ext-apps SDK + MCP bridge
description: Iterating on the viewer UI currently requires: edit code -> npm run build:ui -> mcpb pack -> open .mcpb -> Mat clicks Install -> Mat Cmd+Q and relaunches Claude Desktop -> Mat reproduces bug -> Mat screenshots -> back to me. 5-10 min per cycle. Unworkable for UX polish. \n\nClaude Desktop hardens against CDP automation (codesign entitlements show no disable-library-validation / get-task-allow), so we can't drive the desktop app remotely. But the viewer is a self-contained single-file HTML + TS app — it CAN run in Chrome if we mock the @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps SDK and route app.callServerTool to a local MCP server subprocess. That drops the iteration loop to ~20 seconds and lets an agent use /browse or gstack to drive the viewer directly.
design:
Three files + vite.config + package.json additions.

1) ui/dev/mock-ext-apps.ts — shims the @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps module. Exports App class, McpUiHostContext type, applyDocumentTheme / applyHostStyleVariables noops. App implements: connect() (fires fake host-context event), getHostContext() (returns { tool_input: { pdf_path, display_mode } } from URL query params so you can ?pdf_path=example-fw9.pdf), callServerTool({name,arguments}) (POSTs to /__dev__/tool), sendSizeChanged/updateModelContext/requestDisplayMode (mostly noops that resolve trivially), on(event, fn) (event listener mock).

2) ui/dev/bridge-plugin.mjs — Vite plugin. configureServer hook: spawn  as a child process on startup, attach a simple JSON-RPC correlator over its stdin/stdout (MCP protocol — initialize, initialized, tools/call). Middleware for POST /__dev__/tool that takes {name,arguments}, sends tools/call JSON-RPC to the child, awaits response keyed by rpc id, returns JSON { content, structuredContent, isError }. On server shutdown, kill the child process cleanly.

3) vite.config.mjs — import bridge-plugin.mjs, conditionally add it only when mode==='development'. Add resolve.alias entry to point '@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps' at ui/dev/mock-ext-apps.ts when in dev mode. Keep production build completely untouched — viteSingleFile still produces dist-ui/index.html for mcpb.

4) package.json scripts:  -> . Maybe also  that clears .test-tmp-golden/ and ~/.pdf-toolkit-files/signatures/quick-* so test state resets.

5) ui/dev/index.html (optional) — dev-specific entry if we need to inject ?pdf_path=... defaults. Alternatively just use the existing ui/index.html and read location.search.

When an agent runs , Vite starts at localhost:5173, the MCP server spawns as child of vite, the viewer loads with a default PDF, and every app.callServerTool call round-trips to the real server. Agent drives the viewer via gstack or /browse, captures screenshots, iterates on TS/CSS with instant HMR. No MCPB pack cycle.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] npm run dev:ui starts successfully
- [ ] Viewer at localhost:5173 loads a PDF (e.g. example-fw9.pdf) with no console errors
- [ ] Sign mode works end-to-end: detect_signature_zones returns zones, modal opens, apply_signature stamps, output file lands at expected path on disk
- [ ] Draw-signature modal works (creates a real signature asset via create_signature)
- [ ] Date zone -> apply_text works
- [ ] HMR: editing ui/src/mcp-app.ts reflects in the browser within ~2 seconds
- [ ] Production build still works (npm run build:ui produces dist-ui/index.html with the real ext-apps SDK; the alias is dev-only)
- [ ] mcpb pack still produces a working bundle
- [ ] Bridge cleanly terminates the child MCP server when Vite stops (no orphan processes)
- [ ] Documented in CLAUDE.md or README under 'Local development'

description: Non-blocking follow-ups from Phase B adversarial review. All shipped behavior works correctly after B1-B6 fixes, but these improve robustness + accessibility.
design: (F1) Drawing canvas DPR scaling — resize canvas buffer to CSS * devicePixelRatio on modal open so strokes are crisp on retina and exported PNGs aren't pixelated. (F7) Cache zones keyed by pdfPath — currently refetched on every mode toggle. (F8) When fetchSignatureZones throws, renderSignPanel overwrites the error message with generic 'no zones' empty state — preserve error state until the next successful fetch.

title: Compact mode: declared token-efficiency normalizations
description: Per docs/EXTRACTION_INTELLIGENCE_PLAN_2026-08-03.md section 6: opt-in compact arg; dot-leader collapse, page-number-line removal with isolation context, spaced-hyphen join; per-kind counts + normalized_pages; runs inside the validated render path; full tool-contract wiring incl. fixed digest test. design:
# SPEC B5 — Compact mode normalizations

Bead: pdf-toolkit-mcp-zyx.5. Plan §6. Depends on B3 AND B4 (all renderer gap/result-
shape changes land first — codex review finding 14; renderer already at
1.3.0). Worktree branch: codex/compact-mode.

## Objective

Optional `compact: boolean` (default false) on convert_pdf_to_markdown.
Three deterministic normalizations with per-kind counts in a new
`normalizations` result object. Default output byte-identical to today.

## Design

- Renderer option threaded through renderPdfLayoutToMarkdown; runs INSIDE
  the validated render path so validateMarkdownConversionSemantics
  (markdown-conversion.js:744) re-renders with the same option and
  byte-compares. Table rows and renderLinkedLine outputs are exempt from
  all three normalizations (apply per plain text line during render, not
  as a whole-document regex pass).
- N1 dot_leaders_collapsed: /\.{4,}/g -> " ... " (exactly-3 preserved);
  collapse any resulting double spaces at the splice point only.
- N2 page_number_lines_removed: is_page_number_line port
  (postprocess.rs:187-247): <=4-digit line; "page N [of M]" (case
  insensitive); "N of M"; "-N-". Context rule (postprocess.rs:159-177):
  drop only when isolated between blank/page-boundary lines or directly
  before a page boundary. Removed pages recorded in normalized_pages[].
- N3 spaced_hyphens_joined: letter " - " letter -> letter"-"letter, both
  sides required to be letters (Unicode Letter category — improve on the
  source's hardcoded Latin list; document divergence in a comment).
- Result: normalizations: { dot_leaders_collapsed: int,
  page_number_lines_removed: int, spaced_hyphens_joined: int,
  normalized_pages: int[] } — all zeros/empty when compact=false (schema
  all-required rule).
- FULL tool-contract wiring is this lane's own scope (codex review
  finding 10): advertised inputSchema property (index.js:2678), runtime
  allowedArguments set (index.js:4416), handler forwarding
  (index.js:4489), tool description, output schema entry, the FIXED
  tool-contract digest test (test/mcp-contract.test.js:332 — regenerate
  the digest deliberately), and share mirror.
- No renderer version bump beyond B3's 1.3.0 (same epic bump) UNLESS this
  lane lands first — then it owns the 1.3.0 bump and B3 rides it.

## Acceptance

1. Unit: each normalization boundary-tested (3 vs 4 dots; "12345" kept;
   "42" mid-prose kept, isolated dropped; "- item" list marker safe;
   counts exact; compact=false => byte-identical to pre-change golden
   output for every existing fixture in the suite).
2. Determinism self-check green with compact on and off; double-render
   equality both modes.
3. TOC-style generated fixture end-to-end: exact compact output + counts.
4. `npm test -- test/markdown-conversion.test.js
   test/convert-pdf-to-markdown.test.js test/output-schema.test.js
   test/mcp-contract.test.js` green, then `npm test` green.

## Forbidden

Changing default-mode output by even one byte; touching table/link/heading
logic beyond the exemption guards; layout-extraction.js; new deps;
committing.

title: Offer opt-in XMP ingredient provenance and a sidecar page-source map
description:
Gated behind pdf-toolkit-mcp-igr.17.1. Both surfaces are OFF by default; moving metadata between documents belonging to different parties is a disclosure and must be a choice.

XMP option: record contributing sources with xmpMM:Ingredients and xmpMM:DerivedFrom, the standards vocabulary for a composed asset referencing its components by DocumentID and InstanceID.

HARD CONSTRAINT: never copy source XMP wholesale. Many XMP properties are true only of the document that carried them, including standards-conformance claims such as PDF/A. A merged document almost certainly does not satisfy an inherited conformance claim, so copying the block manufactures exactly the kind of false claim the evaluation contract exists to prevent. Write explicit ingredient references only.

Sidecar option: a companion JSON page-to-source map emitted on merge, for users who intend to split later. Cannot corrupt the PDF and cannot leak into a delivered document. Accepted weakness: it is useless once separated from its PDF and no other tool reads it.

Sources: Adobe Introduction to XMP Asset Relationships; XMP Specification Part 2 Standard Schemas; PDF Association Understanding Private Data in PDF/A (2024-06) and Including custom metadata structures in PDF (2025-10).

title: Bound PDF input reads before parser allocation
description: Mutating tools call fs.readFile before pdf-lib parses the bytes. Very large inputs can allocate unbounded memory before structural validation, and merge has both per-file and aggregate exposure.
design: Establish explicit per-file and aggregate byte limits using opened file handles so size validation and reads share the same identity. Apply one common loader to every PDF-consuming mutation path, preserve same-file/transaction guarantees, and return one stable user-facing resource-limit error.

- [ ] merge_pdfs also enforces a documented aggregate input limit
- [ ] Size checks and reads use the same opened file identity
- [ ] Oversize inputs leave absent and preexisting outputs, backups, and active state unchanged
- [ ] Source/share tests prove clean errors and process liveness

title: Build a native macOS supervisor for bounded structured-extraction evals
description: Build and validate a small hash-bound native supervisor for non-streaming structured-extraction candidates on the designated Apple Silicon evaluation Mac. The supervisor must remain outside a fresh candidate session and process group, install verified inherited kernel backstops before exec, drain bounded output, monitor group membership and resource observations through supported Darwin APIs, enforce a sleep-inclusive deadline, force-terminate on any controller or evidence-integrity failure, prove the original process group empty, and emit only parent-owned evidence. Treat it as an evaluation runner, not a security sandbox or cgroup equivalent.
design: Use a reviewed C supervisor bound into the cross-device receipt by source, compiler command, binary mode, size, and SHA-256. Child calls setsid, installs and reads back RLIMIT_CORE, RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_FSIZE, RLIMIT_NOFILE, and a calibrated per-process RLIMIT_AS tripwire, then execve of the exact pinned Python. Parent uses mach_continuous_time, proc_listpgrppids, proc_listchildpids, proc_pid_rusage, bounded nonblocking pipes, PID plus start-time identity, and killpg with immediate stop and kill on hard breaches. Report sampled group physical footprint and RSS separately. Do not use RLIMIT_RSS as a physical-memory cap, RLIMIT_NPROC under the shared user, launchd as aggregate isolation, or deprecated sandbox-exec as a proof boundary.
acceptance_criteria: On the exact recorded macOS build, conformance tests prove installed hard limits cannot be raised, the calibrated address-space tripwire permits the pinned Docling stack, bounded stdout and stderr cannot deadlock the run, deadlines include system sleep, first controller failure prevents output acceptance, termination proves the original group empty, post-run source/environment/model inventories are reverified, and only schema-valid parent evidence is published. Hostile tests cover rapid memory growth, multiple children, short-lived CPU children, ignored signals, leader exit with live descendants, partial or just-in-time JSON, supervisor crash, enumeration failure, PID reuse, artifact mutation, and escaped sessions. Evidence states that memory and CPU figures are sampled, RLIMIT_AS is per-process virtual address space, and the design does not guarantee zero overshoot, escaped-session containment, cgroup-equivalent isolation, filesystem/network isolation, or safety for hostile code.

title: Evaluate explicit source-aware metadata provenance for merge and split
description: Decide whether PDF Tools should preserve per-input document metadata through merge and later recover it when splitting source-aligned ranges. The current contract uses standard document-level semantics: merge inherits the first input Info dictionary and split inherits its actual input document. Do not add hidden private page dictionaries by default. Research transparent standards-based XMP, PieceInfo, sidecar, privacy, interoperability, and user-control options before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision covers user value, privacy and data-leak risk, PDF interoperability, standards compliance, round-trip behavior, disclosure and opt-in UX, collision handling, and evaluator cases. If adopted, provenance is explicit, inspectable, removable, and tested in at least two independent engines.
notes:
2026-07-25 Claude: closed as an evaluation. Decision recorded in docs/METADATA_PROVENANCE.md; no behavior changed.

MEASURED (through the MCP boundary, not pdf-lib directly): merge inherits the first input's Info and discards the rest; split then copies that Info onto EVERY output regardless of which pages it contains. Inputs A/B merged then split at the source boundary produced pages_3-4 containing only B's pages while reporting Title A / Author A / Subject A / kw-A.

That is the finding: not lost metadata, a false claim. Misattributed authorship is worse than absence for a tool used on contracts and forms, and nothing marks the claim as inherited.

DECISION. Default output stays standards-ordinary. Stop asserting metadata not known to describe the artifact: where merge inputs disagree, omit rather than pick a winner; split must not copy metadata onto ranges whose provenance it cannot establish. Omission over false assertion, consistent with page analysis reporting unknown rather than likely_blank and form validation refusing whole-form readiness claims.

PieceInfo REJECTED PERMANENTLY, not merely by default. Research confirmed general viewers ignore private application data and Acrobat ships a preflight fixup that discards foreign private data, so provenance stored there is invisible and unreliable while still carrying one party's metadata into another party's delivered file.

XMP xmpMM:Ingredients / DerivedFrom accepted as opt-in, with a hard constraint discovered in research: never copy source XMP wholesale, because many properties are true only of the carrying document, including PDF/A conformance claims a merged file does not satisfy. Copying the block would manufacture exactly the false claim the evaluation contract exists to prevent. Sidecar page-source map accepted as the opt-in recovery path. Both default off: moving metadata between parties is a disclosure.

Committed test/metadata-provenance.test.js pinning current behavior including the misattribution case, so the fix has a precise starting point and the finding cannot silently regress. Full suite 1227 passed, 0 failed.

Implementation split out: igr.17.1 (correctness fix, P1) and igr.17.2 (opt-in provenance, P2).

Intended for signatures, handwritten notes, tables, and scanned regions where the model needs visual context without rendering the whole page.
